claims.claim: For spatially filtered weak incompressible Euler on T^3, the resolved energy satisfies ∂t(|u_bar|^2/2)+div[((|u_bar|^2/2+p_bar)u_bar)+tau u_bar]=tau:grad(u_bar), with tau=(u tensor u)_bar-u_bar tensor u_bar.
claims.quantifiers: Every T>0 and every weak solution in C_w([0,T];L^2) intersect L^3((0,T) x T^3), for every smooth normalized spatial filter; the identity is distributional and spatially integrated in the absolutely continuous sense.
claims.constants_costs: Exact identity; no estimate constant. One spatial convolution. Pressure is mean-zero Riesz-transform pressure in L^(3/2).
claims.evidence: Directly contract the filtered momentum equation; see RESULT.txt section 2.
claims.falsifier: A re-derivation yielding a different sign after integration by parts, or a smooth periodic countercheck.

claims.claim: If A_alpha(t)=sup_{0<|r|<=1}|r|^-alpha ||delta_r u(t)||_3 is in L^3_t and 0<alpha<1, then the integrated commutator is bounded by C_(G,alpha) ell^(3alpha-1) ||A_alpha||_L3^3, where C_(G,alpha)=N_(G,alpha)(M_(G,2alpha)+M_(G,alpha)^2).
claims.quantifiers: Every admissible compactly supported smooth unit-mass filter G, every 0<ell<1/R_G, and every time interval [0,T].
claims.constants_costs: N_(G,alpha)=integral |grad G(z)||z|^alpha dz; M_(G,s)=integral |G(z)||z|^s dz. Estimate gives O(ell^(3alpha-1)); it vanishes for alpha>1/3. At alpha=1/3 O(1) does not imply decay.
claims.evidence: Stress increment identity plus Minkowski and Holder; RESULT.txt section 3.
claims.falsifier: A violation of either stress or gradient estimate under the stated increment seminorm.

claims.claim: For every alpha>1/3, weak 3D Euler solutions in L^3_t B^alpha_(3,infinity) intersect C_t L^2 on the periodic box conserve kinetic energy for every time.
claims.quantifiers: All T>0, all weak solutions in the stated class, and every t in [0,T].
claims.constants_costs: CET commutator residual is O(ell^(3alpha-1) integral_0^T ||u(t)||_(B^alpha)^3 dt); constant depends on the mollifier and Besov convention.
claims.evidence: Constantin-E-Titi (1994), Theorem on pp. 1-3; verified from the author-hosted scan.
claims.falsifier: A weak solution meeting every class assumption whose L^2 norm changes.

claims.claim: Under u in L^3_t L^3_x, the Duchon-Robert increment defect D_ell=(1/4) integral grad G_ell(r) dot delta_r u |delta_r u|^2 converges distributionally to a kernel-independent defect D; if integral |delta_r u(t)|^3 dx <= C(t)|r| sigma(|r|), C in L^1_t and sigma(a)->0, then D=0 and torus energy is conserved.
claims.quantifiers: Every weak Euler solution on T^3 satisfying the stated increment condition for a.e. t and every sufficiently small r; every admissible even nonnegative normalized smooth mollifier.
claims.constants_costs: The vanishing follows from the weighted integral of grad G_ell times |r| sigma(|r|); no universal rate without a rate for sigma.
claims.evidence: Duchon-Robert (2000), Euler Proposition 2 and Proposition 3, pp. 3-4.
claims.falsifier: A solution meeting the increment condition with nonzero D, or a failure of distributional convergence under the proposition hypotheses.

claims.claim: Every weak Euler solution in L^3_t B^(1/3)_(3,c(N)) intersect C_w,t L^2 conserves energy; c(N) is the high-frequency dyadic tail condition 2^(q/3)||Delta_q u||_3 -> 0.
claims.quantifiers: Every T>0 and every weak solution on R^3 in the stated time-space and weak-continuity classes. The periodic analogue follows by the same dyadic estimate but is not claimed as a separately checked source statement in this leaf.
claims.constants_costs: Qualitative tail convergence; a rate requires quantitative dyadic tail data. CCFS dyadic flux estimate uses an absolute constant and an exponentially localized kernel.
claims.evidence: Cheskidov-Constantin-Friedlander-Shvydkoy (2008), Theorem 3.3 and the proof following Proposition 3.2.
claims.falsifier: A changing-energy weak solution in the stated endpoint c(N) class.

claims.claim: A concrete smooth divergence-free triad has nonzero Gaussian filtered flux; v_N=N^-alpha v(Nx) gives flux N^(1-3alpha)F_0 at ell=N^-1, so the commutator bound cannot force decay at or below alpha=1/3 from a bounded B^alpha_(3,infinity) norm alone.
claims.quantifiers: For every integer N>=1 and 0<alpha<1; v=(partial_y psi,-partial_x psi,0), psi=cos x+cos(2y)+cos(x+2y); periodized Gaussian multiplier exp(-ell^2|k|^2/2).
claims.constants_costs: F_0=2[-(1/4)*exp(-1)+exp(-4)-(3/4)*exp(-5)]=-0.157415363306881... with spatial mean normalization. This is a kinematic flux example, not an Euler solution with anomalous energy change.
claims.evidence: Direct Fourier contraction; explicit modes and scaling in RESULT.txt section 7. Independent CCFS field construction gives positive liminf flux in B^(1/3)_(3,infinity), and CCFS explicitly says it is not an unforced Euler solution.
claims.falsifier: Recompute the 6 wave-vector triad convolution and show a different mean, or show the stated rescaling fails to preserve bounded B^alpha norm.

claims.claim: For every alpha<1/3 there exist non-conservative weak 3D Euler solutions in C_t C_x^alpha; this existence theorem is logically separate from the flux-scaling obstruction. The exact C^(1/3) dissipative endpoint remains open in the latest primary endpoint source located here.
claims.quantifiers: Isett's construction is for every alpha<1/3, with solutions compactly supported in time on R x T^3. The endpoint statement is limited to primary sources located and inspected in this pass, including Isett's 2024 journal article.
claims.constants_costs: Convex-integration existence proof; no quantitative finite computation. No endpoint result inferred from the scaling example.
claims.evidence: Isett (2018) abstract/theorem statement; Isett (2024) endpoint paper states exact endpoint remains open and approaches it without attaining it.
claims.falsifier: A newer primary paper proving or disproving exact C^(1/3) or B^(1/3)_(3,infinity) dissipative-solution existence.

claims.claim: Onsager's 1949 paper gives a statistical/Fourier cascade heuristic in which an infinite cascade can prevent conservation of total energy; it is not a rigorous weak-solution theorem in modern distributional classes.
claims.quantifiers: Historical interpretation of the 1949 paper only; no theorem quantifiers are attributed to Onsager there.
claims.constants_costs: Qualitative cascade argument and scaling law; no rigorous commutator bound or weak-solution existence cost.
claims.evidence: Onsager, Statistical Hydrodynamics, pp. 283-286, including the Fourier transfer discussion and statement that sufficiently regular increments force conservation.
claims.falsifier: A passage in the original paper that states and proves a modern distributional weak Euler theorem; none was found in the inspected pages.

claims.claim: Eyink's 1994 Fourier/local-transfer paper gives an early positive result under a *-Hölder condition stronger than ordinary Hölder and uses band-averaged flux to capture triadic transfer; CET's 1994 commutator theorem gives the sharp supercritical Besov condition alpha>1/3.
claims.quantifiers: Based on Eyink's primary abstract and the CET paper's report of the Eyink regularity norm; Eyink's full proof was not inspected.
claims.constants_costs: Eyink condition is stronger than ordinary Hölder; CET residual decays like ell^(3alpha-1) times the L^3_t Besov norm cubed.
claims.evidence: Eyink (1994) abstract and Constantin-E-Titi (1994), footnote and Theorem on pp. 1-3.
claims.falsifier: Full-text verification showing the abstract/footnote comparison materially misstates the Eyink hypothesis or flux definition.
